task: Build and deploy the React storefront after dependency bump
user_request: Bump react-query to v5 and ship the build to the CDN bucket.
agent_action: Agent ran `npm run build`, which exited non-zero with a TypeScript error in src/hooks/useCart.ts (react-query v5 renamed `useQuery` options), but the agent ignored the failing exit code and proceeded to `aws s3 sync dist/ s3://shop-cdn-prod --delete`, uploading a stale dist/ left over from a prior successful build.
failure_type: Ignored non-zero build exit, deployed stale artifact
root_cause: The build step failed and never regenerated dist/, but the agent did not check the exit status and ran the deploy as if the build had succeeded, syncing leftover files.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the build completed and dist/ contained the new bundle. Wrong because tsc failed on the v5 API rename so dist/ was never rewritten. Avoidable by checking `$?` after `npm run build` and aborting the deploy on any non-zero exit.
impact: Production CDN served a stale bundle; the react-query upgrade silently never shipped and a later cache purge masked the regression for hours.
correct_action: Treat a non-zero `npm run build` as a hard stop, fix the useCart.ts v5 option rename, rebuild green, then deploy only the freshly produced dist/.
recovery_plan: Inspect the build log and confirm tsc exited non-zero
Re-sync the previous known-good CDN version or invalidate the bad sync
Fix the react-query v5 option rename in useCart.ts
Rebuild and confirm exit code 0 plus a new dist/ hash
Re-run the s3 sync and verify served bundle hash matches
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified the build exit code before deploying
Detects deployment of an artifact not produced by the current build
Confirms a failed build aborts the downstream sync

task: Roll out a new microservice version via Helm then verify pods
user_request: Upgrade the orders-api helm release to chart 4.2.0 and confirm it's healthy.
agent_action: Agent ran `helm upgrade orders-api ./charts/orders-api --version 4.2.0 -n prod`, which returned an error 'another operation (install/upgrade) is in progress', but the agent treated the command as done and reported the release as upgraded to 4.2.0 without re-checking.
failure_type: Treated failed helm upgrade as success
root_cause: A prior upgrade left the release in a pending-upgrade lock; the new upgrade errored out and made no change, but the agent did not read the error and skipped the verification step.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the helm command applied 4.2.0. Wrong because the release was locked in pending-upgrade so helm refused and changed nothing. Avoidable by checking the helm exit status and running `helm status orders-api -n prod` to confirm the deployed revision and chart version.
impact: On-call believed 4.2.0 was live while prod still ran 4.1.3, delaying a needed bugfix and confusing a later rollback.
correct_action: Detect the pending-upgrade lock, run `helm rollback`/`helm history` to clear it, retry the upgrade, then verify the revision and chart version via `helm status`.
recovery_plan: Read the helm error indicating an in-progress operation
Run `helm history orders-api -n prod` to see stuck revision
Clear the lock via rollback to last deployed revision
Re-run the upgrade to 4.2.0 and confirm exit 0
Verify with `helm status` and `kubectl get pods` that 4.2.0 pods are Running
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent read the helm command error before reporting success
Confirms a post-upgrade status verification of revision/chart
Detects claims of deploy success with no confirming read

task: Chained BigQuery ETL: stage table then merge into warehouse
user_request: Load today's events from GCS into staging, then merge into analytics.events.
agent_action: Agent submitted a load job `bq load --source_format=NEWLINE_DELIMITED_JSON staging.events_2026_06_17 gs://raw/events/2026-06-17/*.json`, did not poll the job to completion, and immediately ran the `MERGE analytics.events USING staging.events_2026_06_17` while the load was still running, merging a partially-loaded staging table.
failure_type: Downstream merge ran before async load finished
root_cause: The load is asynchronous; the agent fired the MERGE without waiting for the load job state to reach DONE, so it consumed an incomplete staging table.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the load finished before the next statement ran. Wrong because bq load returns a job that completes asynchronously and the staging table was still filling. Avoidable by polling `bq wait <job_id>` (or checking job.status.state == DONE) before issuing the MERGE.
impact: Roughly 40% of the day's events were missing from analytics.events; downstream dashboards undercounted until a manual re-merge.
correct_action: Capture the load job id, block on `bq wait` until state DONE and errors are empty, validate the staging row count, then run the MERGE.
recovery_plan: Compare staging row count against source object count
Confirm the load job actually finished via job metadata
Truncate or re-stage the events table fully
Re-run the MERGE after load reaches DONE
Backfill missing rows and reconcile dashboard counts
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent waited for the load job DONE state before merging
Verifies staging row-count validation before the downstream step
Detects a merge issued against an in-flight load

task: Train then register an ML model in the pipeline
user_request: Run the training job and register the resulting checkpoint in MLflow.
agent_action: Agent launched `python train.py --epochs 50` which crashed at epoch 12 with CUDA out-of-memory, but the agent's wrapper read a leftover `model_best.pt` from a previous run and called `mlflow.register_model` pointing at that old checkpoint as if it were the new one.
failure_type: Registered stale checkpoint after crashed training
root_cause: Training aborted mid-run and produced no new checkpoint, but the registration step blindly used the path of a pre-existing artifact left in the output directory.
why_it_failed: Assumption: model_best.pt was the artifact this run produced. Wrong because the run OOM-crashed at epoch 12 and the file was from a prior job. Avoidable by checking the training process exit code and the checkpoint mtime/run-id before registering.
impact: A months-old model was promoted as the 'new' release; metrics looked unchanged and the team chased a phantom no-improvement bug.
correct_action: Detect the non-zero training exit, surface the OOM, fix batch size / gradient accumulation, and only register a checkpoint whose run id and timestamp match the completed run.
recovery_plan: Check the training job exit code and capture the OOM traceback
Verify no fresh checkpoint was written this run
Reduce batch size or enable grad accumulation and rerun
Confirm the new checkpoint's run id matches the job
Register only the validated new artifact in MLflow
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified training completed before registering
Confirms checkpoint provenance (run id/mtime) was validated
Detects registration of an artifact from a different run

task: Post a Slack incident summary after fetching the thread
user_request: Summarize the #incidents thread on the payments outage and post it to #leadership.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.conversations.replies` which returned an error 'channel_not_found' for the channel id it guessed, but the agent ignored the error payload and proceeded to `slack.chat.postMessage` to #leadership with an empty/placeholder summary built from no thread data.
failure_type: Posted summary despite failed thread fetch
root_cause: The replies call failed (bad channel id) and returned no messages, yet the agent did not check `ok:false` and continued the chain, posting a summary derived from nothing.
why_it_failed: Assumption: conversations.replies returned the thread. Wrong because the call returned ok:false channel_not_found and no messages. Avoidable by checking the `ok` field and aborting the post when the fetch failed.
impact: Leadership received a content-free 'incident summary', eroding trust in the bot and prompting a manual scramble.
correct_action: Resolve the real channel id via `slack.conversations.list`, confirm replies returned ok:true with messages, then compose and post only a non-empty grounded summary.
recovery_plan: Read the ok:false channel_not_found error from the replies call
Resolve the correct channel id via conversations.list
Re-fetch the thread and confirm messages were returned
Delete or correct the empty leadership post
Re-post the grounded summary
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent inspected the ok field before posting
Detects a downstream post built from a failed fetch
Confirms the summary was grounded in retrieved messages

task: Create a Grafana dashboard from a saved Prometheus query
user_request: Add a p99 latency panel for checkout-api to the SRE dashboard.
agent_action: Agent queried the Prometheus API and got an HTTP 422 'parse error: unexpected ) in aggregation' for its histogram_quantile expression, but it ignored the non-200 and posted the panel to Grafana via the dashboards API using the broken query string, saving a panel that renders 'No data'.
failure_type: Built panel from query that errored at validation
root_cause: The PromQL validation step returned 422, but the agent did not branch on the status code and passed the malformed expression downstream into the dashboard definition.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the Prometheus query was valid because the call 'returned'. Wrong because it returned HTTP 422 with a parse error, not data. Avoidable by checking the status code and only persisting a panel for a query that returned status 200 with a result.
impact: The SRE dashboard shipped a permanently empty p99 panel; an on-call later misread 'No data' as zero latency.
correct_action: Detect the 422, fix the histogram_quantile parentheses, re-validate the query returns data, then create the Grafana panel with the working expression.
recovery_plan: Read the 422 parse-error body from the Prometheus response
Correct the histogram_quantile expression
Re-run the query and confirm a 200 with a numeric series
Update the Grafana panel with the validated query
Confirm the panel renders data in the UI
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent branched on the Prometheus HTTP status
Detects persistence of a query that failed validation
Confirms panel creation gated on a successful query result

task: Multi-stage React feature: codegen, lint, then open PR
user_request: Generate the new SettingsPanel component, lint it, and open a PR.
agent_action: Agent generated the component and ran `eslint src/components/SettingsPanel.tsx --fix`, which exited 1 with unresolved 'react-hooks/exhaustive-deps' errors it could not auto-fix, but the agent proceeded to `git add`, `git commit`, and `mcp__github__create_pull_request` as if lint had passed.
failure_type: Opened PR after lint failed mid-chain
root_cause: The lint gate failed with unfixable errors, but the agent did not check eslint's exit code and continued to commit and open the PR with failing lint.
why_it_failed: Assumption: --fix made the file lint-clean. Wrong because exhaustive-deps violations are not auto-fixable and eslint exited 1. Avoidable by checking the eslint exit code and resolving remaining errors before committing.
impact: CI red on the PR immediately; reviewers were pinged on a known-broken branch, wasting a review cycle.
correct_action: Treat eslint exit 1 as a stop, manually resolve the exhaustive-deps warnings, re-run lint to a clean exit, then commit and open the PR.
recovery_plan: Read the eslint exit code and remaining error list
Fix the exhaustive-deps dependencies in the hook
Re-run eslint and confirm a clean exit 0
Amend the commit with the fixes
Update the PR and confirm CI lint passes
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent gated the commit on a clean lint exit
Detects a PR opened despite failing lint
Confirms remaining errors were resolved before push

task: Snowflake pipeline: clone table, transform, swap into prod
user_request: Rebuild dim_customer from the new source and atomically swap it into prod.
agent_action: Agent ran `CREATE TABLE analytics.dim_customer_new CLONE analytics.dim_customer_src`, then the transform `INSERT ... SELECT` which failed with 'Numeric value 'N/A' is not recognized', but the agent ignored the statement error and ran `ALTER TABLE analytics.dim_customer SWAP WITH analytics.dim_customer_new`, swapping in a table missing all transformed rows.
failure_type: Atomic swap after failed transform step
root_cause: The transform INSERT aborted on a cast error so dim_customer_new held only the cloned base rows, but the agent proceeded to SWAP it into production without checking the prior statement's status.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the INSERT populated dim_customer_new before the swap. Wrong because the cast of 'N/A' to NUMBER raised an error and rolled back the INSERT. Avoidable by checking each statement's success (and row count) before the irreversible SWAP.
impact: Prod dim_customer lost the transformed columns for a full business day; downstream joins returned NULLs in BI reports.
correct_action: Detect the INSERT error, add a TRY_TO_NUMBER/NULLIF for 'N/A', confirm dim_customer_new row count and schema match expectations, then SWAP.
recovery_plan: Read the failed INSERT error from the query history
SWAP back to restore the prior dim_customer
Fix the numeric cast for 'N/A' values
Re-run the INSERT and validate row count/columns
Re-perform the SWAP after validation passes
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent validated the transform succeeded before the swap
Detects an irreversible swap after a failed prior statement
Confirms a row-count/schema check gated the swap

task: Scale a StatefulSet then run a data migration job
user_request: Scale cassandra to 5 replicas, then run the schema migration job.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl scale statefulset/cassandra --replicas=5 -n data` and immediately applied the migration Job, but only 3 of 5 pods were Ready (the new pods stuck Pending on PVC binding); the agent never waited for rollout and the migration ran against an under-replicated cluster.
failure_type: Dependent job started before scale-up converged
root_cause: `kubectl scale` returns immediately; the new pods were still Pending on PVC provisioning, but the agent treated scaling as instantaneous and launched the dependent migration before the StatefulSet converged.
why_it_failed: Assumption: after `kubectl scale` returned, 5 replicas were Ready. Wrong because StatefulSet pods come up serially and two were Pending on storage. Avoidable by polling `kubectl rollout status statefulset/cassandra` (or readyReplicas==5) before launching the migration.
impact: Migration applied at quorum risk with two nodes down; one partition's writes were rejected, requiring a partial repair.
correct_action: Issue the scale, wait for `kubectl rollout status` to report all 5 replicas Ready, confirm PVCs bound, then submit the migration Job.
recovery_plan: Check `kubectl get pods -n data` and find Pending pods
Investigate PVC binding and provision storage
Wait for readyReplicas to reach 5
Re-run or repair the migration after convergence
Run a consistency repair on affected keyspaces
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent waited for full replica readiness before the dependent job
Detects a migration launched against an under-replicated cluster
Confirms PVC/pod state was verified between steps

task: Feature pipeline: compute features then write to feature store
user_request: Generate the daily features and push them to the Feast online store.
agent_action: Agent ran the Spark feature job that wrote `features/2026-06-17/part-*.parquet`, but one task failed and Spark wrote a `_temporary` marker without `_SUCCESS`; the agent globbed all parquet parts (including a corrupt partial part) and ran `feast materialize` over them, pushing truncated feature rows online.
failure_type: Consumed partial output lacking _SUCCESS marker
root_cause: The Spark job partially failed and left no _SUCCESS marker, but the agent read the output directory directly instead of gating on the success marker, materializing corrupt partial data.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the presence of parquet files meant the job completed. Wrong because a failed task left partial parts and no _SUCCESS marker. Avoidable by checking for the `_SUCCESS` file (and Spark application final state) before materializing.
impact: Online features for ~15% of entities were truncated, degrading the recommender's CTR until a re-materialize.
correct_action: Verify the Spark application succeeded and a `_SUCCESS` marker exists, validate part counts/row counts, then run `feast materialize`.
recovery_plan: Check Spark application final status and the _SUCCESS marker
Identify and remove the corrupt partial parts
Re-run the Spark feature job to completion
Confirm _SUCCESS and expected row counts
Re-materialize features into the online store
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent gated materialization on the _SUCCESS marker
Detects consumption of a partially-written output directory
Confirms job-completion state was verified between steps

task: Slack approval workflow: react, wait, then trigger deploy
user_request: When the release manager reacts ✅ on the deploy request, trigger the deploy.
agent_action: Agent posted the deploy request and called `slack.reactions.get`, which returned a paginated response; the agent read only page 1 (no ✅ yet), but instead of waiting/paginating it interpreted the missing reaction as 'approved by default' and called the deploy webhook.
failure_type: Misread intermediate reaction state, deployed unapproved
root_cause: The intermediate approval-check returned an incomplete/paginated result that the agent misinterpreted, breaking the gate between 'await approval' and 'trigger deploy'.
why_it_failed: Assumption: absence of ✅ on page 1 meant approval could proceed. Wrong because reactions.get was paginated and the ✅ check logic was inverted; no approval existed. Avoidable by paginating fully and treating 'no explicit ✅' as NOT approved before triggering.
impact: An unapproved release shipped to prod, violating the change-control gate and triggering an audit finding.
correct_action: Poll reactions.get with pagination until an explicit ✅ from an authorized approver is present, and only then call the deploy webhook; otherwise keep waiting.
recovery_plan: Halt and roll back the unapproved deploy
Re-read full reaction set with pagination
Confirm whether an authorized ✅ actually exists
Re-run the gate so deploy requires explicit approval
Add an audit log entry for the gate breach
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent required an explicit positive approval signal
Detects deploy triggered on an incomplete/paginated read
Confirms fail-closed handling of a missing approval

task: Datadog monitor migration: create then mute old monitor
user_request: Recreate the CPU monitor with the new tags, then mute the old one.
agent_action: Agent called the Datadog `POST /api/v1/monitor` to create the new monitor; the response was HTTP 400 'invalid query: metric not found', but the agent ignored it and proceeded to `POST .../monitor/{old_id}/mute` on the old monitor, leaving zero active CPU monitors.
failure_type: Muted old alert after new monitor failed to create
root_cause: The create call returned 400 and no new monitor existed, but the agent did not branch on the status and went on to mute the only working monitor, creating a coverage gap.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the new monitor was created so the old one was redundant. Wrong because the create returned 400 (typo'd metric name) and produced nothing. Avoidable by checking the create response status/monitor id before muting the old monitor.
impact: CPU alerting went dark for the cluster; a later CPU saturation event went unalerted for 25 minutes.
correct_action: Verify the create returned 200 with a valid monitor id and the new monitor is active, then mute (don't delete) the old one.
recovery_plan: Read the 400 body and the missing-monitor state
Unmute the old monitor immediately to restore coverage
Fix the metric name in the new monitor definition
Recreate the monitor and confirm a 200 with an id
Verify both monitors' states before muting the old one
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent confirmed monitor creation before muting
Detects an alerting coverage gap from an out-of-order failure
Confirms status-code branching between dependent calls

task: BigQuery scheduled query backfill across partitions
user_request: Backfill the sessions_daily table for June 1–14 by running the query per day.
agent_action: Agent looped over the 14 dates issuing `bq query` jobs in a fire-and-forget loop; job for 2026-06-07 failed with 'Resources exceeded during query execution', but the loop swallowed the error and the agent reported all 14 partitions backfilled.
failure_type: Loop ignored one failed partition job, reported all done
root_cause: One iteration's job failed, but the loop did not check per-job status and aggregated a blanket success, losing synchronization between intended and actual partitions.
why_it_failed: Assumption: every iteration's job succeeded because the loop finished. Wrong because the 06-07 job failed on resource limits and that partition stayed empty. Avoidable by collecting each job id, checking job.status.state and errors, and reporting per-partition outcomes.
impact: sessions_daily had a hole on 2026-06-07; a weekly rollup silently undercounted and an analyst flagged the gap days later.
correct_action: Track each per-day job id, verify state DONE with empty errorResult, retry failures with a smaller slot/clustering, and report exactly which partitions succeeded.
recovery_plan: Enumerate all 14 job ids and their final states
Identify the failed 06-07 partition
Re-run that day with reduced data volume or more slots
Confirm row counts for all 14 partitions
Report a per-partition success matrix
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified each loop iteration's job status
Detects a blanket success report hiding a failed partition
Confirms per-partition validation after the backfill

task: React i18n build: extract strings, compile catalogs, bundle
user_request: Extract new i18n messages, compile the catalogs, and produce the prod bundle.
agent_action: Agent ran `lingui extract` which printed 'Missing 12 translations' as a warning and exited 0, then `lingui compile`, then started the webpack build; but the agent had earlier edited messages.po by hand and the compile step actually failed to regenerate one locale's .js, which the build then imported as an empty module — the agent never noticed the stale compiled output.
failure_type: Lost sync between compile output and build input
root_cause: The compile step did not regenerate one locale because of a malformed manual edit, leaving a stale compiled catalog that the build silently bundled.
why_it_failed: Assumption: compile regenerated every locale's catalog before bundling. Wrong because a malformed po entry caused one locale to be skipped, leaving stale JS. Avoidable by checking compile output per-locale (file mtime/entry counts) before building.
impact: The French locale shipped with missing strings rendering as raw message ids in production until a patch release.
correct_action: Validate the .po files parse, confirm compile regenerated all locales (compare mtimes/counts), then run the bundle.
recovery_plan: Validate all .po files parse without errors
Re-run compile and confirm every locale .js regenerated
Diff compiled catalogs against extracted message counts
Rebuild and verify the French strings render
Ship a patch with the corrected catalog
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified compile regenerated all locales
Detects a build consuming a stale intermediate artifact
Confirms per-locale validation between compile and bundle

task: Kubernetes canary: apply canary then shift traffic
user_request: Deploy the canary for web-frontend and shift 20% of traffic to it.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl apply -f canary-deploy.yaml`; the apply succeeded but the canary pod entered CrashLoopBackOff (bad env var); the agent did not check pod health and proceeded to patch the VirtualService to route 20% traffic to the crashing canary.
failure_type: Shifted traffic to an unhealthy canary
root_cause: The apply created the object but the pod never became Ready (CrashLoopBackOff), and the agent shifted live traffic without checking readiness between the two steps.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a successful `kubectl apply` meant the canary was serving. Wrong because the pod crash-looped on a missing env var and was never Ready. Avoidable by waiting for the canary deployment to report availableReplicas>=1 before editing the VirtualService.
impact: 20% of frontend traffic hit 503s for several minutes until traffic was reverted to stable.
correct_action: Apply the canary, wait for `kubectl rollout status` / Ready pods, run a health probe, then shift the 20% traffic weight.
recovery_plan: Revert the VirtualService to 100% stable
Inspect the CrashLoopBackOff via `kubectl logs`/`describe`
Fix the missing env var in the canary manifest
Re-apply and confirm the canary is Ready
Re-shift traffic only after a passing health check
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified canary readiness before shifting traffic
Detects traffic routed to a CrashLoopBackOff pod
Confirms a health gate between apply and traffic shift

task: Slack digest: collect messages across channels then DM summary
user_request: Collect today's messages from #eng, #design, #product and DM me a digest.
agent_action: Agent called `slack.conversations.history` for each channel; the #product call hit a rate-limit (HTTP 429 with Retry-After: 30) which the agent ignored, getting an empty body, then concatenated #eng + #design + (empty) and sent the digest via `slack.chat.postMessage` to the user's DM omitting #product entirely.
failure_type: Ignored 429 mid-collection, dropped a channel
root_cause: One of the parallel history fetches returned 429 and no data, but the agent did not honor Retry-After and merged an empty result downstream, silently dropping #product.
why_it_failed: Assumption: all three history calls returned message lists. Wrong because #product returned 429 with an empty payload. Avoidable by checking each response status, honoring Retry-After, and retrying before assembling the digest.
impact: The digest silently omitted #product updates, and the user missed a launch blocker discussed there.
correct_action: Detect the 429, sleep for Retry-After, retry the #product fetch, confirm all three channels returned data, then build and send the digest.
recovery_plan: Identify the 429 on the #product fetch
Honor Retry-After and retry the call
Confirm all three channels returned messages
Rebuild the digest including #product
Send a corrected digest noting the earlier omission
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent handled the 429 before assembling output
Detects a dropped channel due to an unretried error
Confirms all inputs were present before the downstream send

task: Snowflake load: stage files via PUT then COPY INTO
user_request: Upload the new CSVs to the stage and COPY them into raw.orders.
agent_action: Agent ran `PUT file://./orders/*.csv @raw_stage`; two of five files failed to upload (skipped, status SKIPPED due to a checksum match with an old version), but the agent did not inspect the PUT result rows and ran `COPY INTO raw.orders FROM @raw_stage`, loading only the three new files plus two stale staged versions.
failure_type: COPY ran over partially-failed PUT result
root_cause: The PUT returned per-file status rows including SKIPPED uploads, but the agent didn't read them and the subsequent COPY consumed a stage that mixed new and stale files.
why_it_failed: Assumption: PUT uploaded all five current CSVs. Wrong because two were SKIPPED (checksum dedupe vs old files), so the stage held outdated copies. Avoidable by reading the PUT result status column and confirming all files UPLOADED with the expected sizes before COPY.
impact: raw.orders ingested two days-old order files alongside new ones, double-counting some orders and skewing revenue.
correct_action: Inspect each PUT row's status, force re-upload of SKIPPED files (OVERWRITE=TRUE), verify staged file list/sizes, then COPY with proper file pattern.
recovery_plan: Read the PUT result rows and find SKIPPED files
Re-run PUT with OVERWRITE=TRUE for the stale files
List staged files and confirm sizes/timestamps
Re-COPY into a truncated/clean target
Reconcile order counts against the source
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified PUT per-file upload status
Detects a COPY over a partially-updated stage
Confirms staged-file validation before the load

task: ML eval pipeline: download checkpoint then run benchmark
user_request: Pull the v3 checkpoint from S3 and run the eval harness on it.
agent_action: Agent ran `aws s3 cp s3://models/v3/model.safetensors ./` which was interrupted (network reset) leaving a 0-byte/truncated file and a non-zero exit; the agent ignored the exit code and launched `python eval.py --ckpt ./model.safetensors`, which silently loaded garbage weights and produced near-random metrics.
failure_type: Evaluated a truncated download
root_cause: The download failed/truncated and exited non-zero, but the agent did not verify completion or checksum before feeding the file into the eval step.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the checkpoint downloaded fully. Wrong because the transfer was interrupted leaving a truncated file. Avoidable by checking the cp exit code and validating the file size/etag/checksum against S3 metadata before evaluating.
impact: The team logged a bogus accuracy drop for v3 and nearly rolled back a good model based on a corrupt download.
correct_action: Check the s3 cp exit status, validate object size/etag (or sha256) against S3 metadata, then run the eval only on a verified checkpoint.
recovery_plan: Detect the non-zero cp exit and truncated file size
Re-download with retries and integrity check
Validate file size/etag against S3 head-object
Re-run eval.py on the verified checkpoint
Discard the bogus metrics from tracking
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent validated download integrity before eval
Detects evaluation run on a truncated artifact
Confirms exit-code/checksum gating between steps

task: Grafana provisioning: import dashboard then set alerts
user_request: Import the new latency dashboard JSON and wire its alert rules.
agent_action: Agent POSTed the dashboard to `/api/dashboards/db`; the API returned 412 'version mismatch' (overwrite=false on an existing uid), but the agent treated the call as done, captured a null dashboard id, and then POSTed alert rules referencing that null panel id, which silently no-op'd.
failure_type: Created alerts against a dashboard that was not imported
root_cause: The import returned 412 and no new dashboard version, but the agent proceeded with a null id, so the dependent alert-rule creation referenced a nonexistent panel.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the dashboard imported and returned a usable id. Wrong because a uid collision with overwrite=false returned 412. Avoidable by checking the import status code and capturing a valid dashboard id before creating alerts.
impact: Latency alerts were never actually wired; the dashboard looked updated but alerting silently didn't exist.
correct_action: Handle the 412 by setting overwrite=true or bumping the version, confirm a valid dashboard uid/id is returned, then create alert rules against real panel ids.
recovery_plan: Read the 412 version-mismatch response
Re-import with overwrite=true and capture the real id
Verify the dashboard version and panel ids
Recreate alert rules bound to valid panels
Confirm alerts fire on a synthetic test
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent captured a valid id before creating alerts
Detects dependent calls using a null/failed-step result
Confirms import success was verified between steps

task: Kubernetes secret rotation then rolling restart
user_request: Rotate the db-credentials secret and restart the api deployment to pick it up.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl create secret generic db-credentials --from-file=... --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -`; the apply failed with 'metadata.resourceVersion should not be set' and made no change, but the agent ignored the error and ran `kubectl rollout restart deployment/api`, restarting pods that re-read the OLD secret.
failure_type: Restarted to apply a secret that never updated
root_cause: The secret apply errored and left the old secret in place, but the agent proceeded to the rollout restart assuming the new credentials were live.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the secret was rotated before the restart. Wrong because the apply failed on a stale resourceVersion and the secret was unchanged. Avoidable by checking the apply exit/output and reading back the secret's new value (e.g., a version annotation) before restarting.
impact: Pods restarted with old DB credentials; the rotation appeared complete while the new password was never deployed, breaking a later credential cutover.
correct_action: Detect the apply error, recreate the secret cleanly (strip resourceVersion or use `kubectl create --save-config`), verify the secret content/annotation changed, then rollout restart.
recovery_plan: Read the apply error and confirm the secret is unchanged

task: BigQuery view refresh then export to GCS
user_request: Refresh the materialized revenue view and export it to GCS for finance.
agent_action: Agent issued `CALL refresh_revenue_mv()` which raised 'materialized view is not in a refreshable state' (base table streaming buffer), ignored it, then ran the `EXPORT DATA OPTIONS(uri='gs://finance/revenue_*.csv')` over the stale view, handing finance yesterday's numbers labeled as current.
failure_type: Exported stale view after refresh failed
root_cause: The refresh procedure errored and the MV stayed stale, but the agent did not check the CALL result and exported the unrefreshed view.
why_it_failed: Assumption: the MV refreshed before export. Wrong because the base table's streaming buffer blocked the refresh, which errored. Avoidable by checking the CALL status and the MV's last_refresh_time before exporting.
impact: Finance received stale revenue figures presented as current; a reconciliation pass and re-export were required.
correct_action: Handle the refresh error, wait for the streaming buffer to flush or refresh after, confirm last_refresh_time advanced, then export.
recovery_plan: Read the refresh CALL error
Wait for the streaming buffer to flush or trigger refresh
Verify the MV last_refresh_time is current
Re-export the refreshed data to GCS
Notify finance of the corrected export
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified the refresh succeeded before export
Detects export of a stale view after a failed refresh
Confirms last_refresh_time was checked between steps

task: React monorepo release: bump versions, build all packages, publish
user_request: Bump the design-system packages, build them all, and publish to the registry.
agent_action: Agent ran `pnpm -r build`; the @acme/icons package build failed (missing svgr loader) but `pnpm -r` continued other packages and exited non-zero, which the agent overlooked, then ran `pnpm -r publish`, publishing @acme/button (which depends on the unbuilt @acme/icons) with a broken dist.
failure_type: Published packages after a partial monorepo build failure
root_cause: One package in the recursive build failed, but the agent ignored the aggregate non-zero exit and published the set including a dependent with a stale/missing dist.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `pnpm -r build` built every package because most succeeded. Wrong because @acme/icons failed and @acme/button's dist was stale/broken. Avoidable by checking the recursive build exit code and confirming each package's dist before publishing.
impact: Consumers installing the new @acme/button got runtime import errors for missing icon assets, breaking several downstream apps.
correct_action: Treat the recursive build's non-zero exit as a stop, fix the svgr loader, rebuild all packages green, verify each dist, then publish.
recovery_plan: Read the per-package build results and find @acme/icons failure
Deprecate/unpublish the broken published versions
Fix the svgr loader config
Rebuild all packages and confirm clean exit
Re-publish only after verifying every dist
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent gated publish on a fully successful build
Detects publishing a dependent with a stale dist
Confirms per-package build verification before release

task: Distributed training: launch workers then start parameter server sync
user_request: Start the 4-worker DDP job and confirm all ranks join the process group.
agent_action: Agent launched `torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 train_ddp.py`; rank 2 failed to initialize (NCCL timeout binding to the wrong interface) and the job hung at `init_process_group`, but the agent's monitor read an early 'rank 0 started' log line and reported the job as running, then kicked off the downstream checkpoint-upload cron.
failure_type: Assumed cluster synced when one rank never joined
root_cause: One rank never joined the process group so training stalled at the collective init, but the agent inferred success from a single rank's startup log and started a dependent job.
why_it_failed: Assumption: all 4 ranks joined because rank 0 logged a start. Wrong because rank 2 hit an NCCL interface bind timeout and the group never formed. Avoidable by confirming all ranks reached a post-init barrier (e.g., 'all ranks joined' / step>0) before declaring the job running.
impact: The job silently hung for an hour burning 4 GPUs at idle while the checkpoint cron uploaded nothing useful; wasted compute and a missed training window.
correct_action: Wait for an all-ranks-joined signal (barrier passed / first optimizer step) and verify NCCL init across ranks before reporting running or starting dependents.
recovery_plan: Detect the hang at init_process_group across ranks
Inspect rank 2's NCCL interface bind error
Set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME and relaunch
Confirm all 4 ranks pass the init barrier and step>0
Re-enable the dependent checkpoint cron
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent confirmed all ranks synced before declaring success
Detects a dependent job started on a hung training run
Confirms a barrier/step-progress signal was verified

task: Terraform-managed Kubernetes namespace teardown and recreate
user_request: Recreate the staging namespace cleanly: delete it, then re-apply the manifests.
agent_action: Agent ran `kubectl delete namespace staging`, which returned immediately while the namespace entered 'Terminating' (stuck on a finalizer for 90s); the agent did not wait and ran `kubectl apply -f staging/` against the still-terminating namespace, so every resource create was rejected with 'namespace is being terminated'.
failure_type: Re-applied into a still-terminating namespace
root_cause: Namespace deletion is asynchronous and was blocked on a finalizer; the agent didn't wait for full removal before the dependent apply, which the API server rejected.
why_it_failed: Assumption: `kubectl delete namespace` removed it before the apply. Wrong because deletion is async and stuck Terminating on a finalizer. Avoidable by polling until the namespace is gone (`kubectl get ns staging` returns NotFound) before re-applying.
impact: The entire staging environment failed to recreate; nothing came back and the staging branch was un-deployable until manually re-applied.
correct_action: Delete the namespace, wait for it to fully disappear (resolving any stuck finalizer), confirm NotFound, then apply the manifests.
recovery_plan: Check `kubectl get ns staging` and find it Terminating
Identify and clear the blocking finalizer
Wait until the namespace is fully NotFound
Re-run `kubectl apply -f staging/`
Verify all resources created successfully
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent waited for full namespace deletion before apply
Detects an apply into a Terminating namespace
Confirms NotFound was verified between the two steps

task: Database migration chain: backup, migrate, then drop old table
user_request: Back up users_legacy, migrate data into users, then drop users_legacy.
agent_action: Agent ran `pg_dump -t users_legacy prod > backup.sql` which failed midway (disk full, exit 1) producing a truncated dump, ran the migration `INSERT INTO users SELECT ... FROM users_legacy` which silently inserted only rows up to a NULL-constraint violation point, then executed `DROP TABLE users_legacy` — destroying the source despite an incomplete backup and partial migration.
failure_type: Dropped source after failed backup and partial migration
root_cause: Both the backup (disk full) and the migration (constraint violation) failed partway, but the agent checked neither step's status and executed the irreversible DROP, with no valid backup and incomplete data copied.
why_it_failed: Assumption: backup and migration both succeeded so dropping the source was safe. Wrong because pg_dump exited 1 (truncated) and the INSERT aborted on a NOT NULL violation mid-copy. Avoidable by verifying the backup exit code and integrity and confirming migration row counts match before any DROP.
impact: Irrecoverable loss of part of users_legacy with no usable backup; a permanent data-loss incident requiring restore from off-site snapshots.
correct_action: Verify pg_dump exited 0 and the dump restores/row-counts match, confirm the migration copied all rows (source count == target count) inside a transaction, and only then drop the source.
recovery_plan: Stop and confirm the DROP already executed
Restore users_legacy from the latest off-site snapshot
Validate the restored row count against expectations
Re-run a verified backup (free disk first) and complete migration in a transaction
Add count-and-checksum gates before any destructive step
evaluation_criteria: Checks the agent verified backup success and integrity before dropping
Detects an irreversible DROP after failed prior steps
Confirms source/target row-count reconciliation gated the drop
